prs.title: fix(scale): Redis never serves an anchor older than Mongo after a field update, a re-save or a late refill (#9840)
prs.summary: On three paths, Redis was written with a request's own copy of an anchor, and that copy could be older than what Mongo held. A, field update:

prs.title: fix(scale): Redis never serves an anchor older than Mongo after a field update or a late refill (#9840)
prs.summary: Redis could hold an older copy of a node than Mongo, and every later read returned that stale copy. A.

prs.title: fix(seal): bake a serve manifest free of seal stage paths
prs.summary: The baked serve manifest recorded the temporary seal folder, for example `/tmp/jac-app-precompile-<pid>-<random>/app`. You changed `build_serve_manifest` in `jac/jaclang/dist/seal.jac`.

prs.title: fix(scale): Redis never serves an anchor older than Mongo after a field update or a late refill (#9840)
prs.summary: On the 0.34.x line, Redis could end up holding an older copy of a node than Mongo, and every later read got that stale copy. A field-only save

prs.title: fix(serve): pool and reuse keep-alive connections in the serving client (#7907)
prs.summary: Before this PR, the client never reused a connection. The PR keeps idle keep-alive connections in a per-event-loop pool, keyed by origin, and reuses a connection only when the previous response was cleanly framed and fully read.

prs.title: feat(scale): the admin Logs page reads pod logs when Loki is not deployed (#9673)
prs.summary: Loki With logs off, there was no Loki to ask, so the Logs page always answered `502 Log backend unavailable`, and nothing in `scale/` could read pod logs another way.

prs.title: fix(scale): Prometheus scrapes every app pod and gateway replica (#9672)
prs.summary: Before this PR, Prometheus had exactly one scrape target: the static address `gateway-service:<port>`. You replaced the static target with Kubernetes pod discovery (`kubernetes_sd_configs` with `role: pod`), limited to the deploy namespace.

prs.title: fix(scale): build deployed pods from the app's [serve] config, not the deployer's (#9382)
prs.summary: Since #8981 (release 0.37.5), those settings came from the process running the deploy, not from the app being deployed. You replaced `_serve_settings()` with `_serve_config()`.

prs.title: fix(scale): add the default memory HPA trigger only when memory_request is configured
prs.summary: request The guard that decides whether to add the memory metric, `has_memory_request`, was computed after that fallback, so it was always true, and every HPA got a memory metric based on a request nobody chose.

prs.title: fix(seal): bake a serve manifest free of seal stage paths
prs.summary: The baked manifest recorded that temporary stage path, both as the manifest's `root` and as each surface entry's `module`. You fixed it by having `build_serve_manifest` drop `root` from every baked manifest and `module` from every surface entry, so the baked file holds no stage path.

prs.title: fix(scale): fail the pack when the seal leaves no serving metadata (#9138)
prs.summary: The host could pack and ship a `.jab` with no `.jac/serve_manifest.json`, report success, and leave every pod to crash at boot with `Error loading web/main.jac: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../.jac/serve_manifest.json'`. You added one host-side check, `require_serve_manifest`, and call it after the bake and in the tar step.

prs.title: fix(scale): keep the minted JWT signing secret across redeploys (#9080)
prs.summary: The bug: a new random secret was minted on every deploy and written over the live Secret. The fix: the manifest builder now renders a fixed placeholder (`PLACEHOLDER_JWT_SECRET`) instead of a random value.

prs.title: fix(serve): derive file ETags from content so a redeploy revalidates onto the new page shell (#9195)
prs.summary: ETag The ETag was built from the file's modified time and size.

prs.title: fix(scale): deploy a workspace from its project root (#9256)
prs.summary: The bug: the deploy chose the folder that holds the entry file (`web/`), not the project root. The fix: a new helper, `deployed_tree`, returns the project root as the folder to ship when the project is a workspace.

prs.title: fix(runtime): stamp the serve manifest format and refuse a skewed bundle (#9140)
prs.summary: The file never said which layout it used, so a bundle built by one jac and booted by another either crashed with an unrelated error (`Error loading main.jac: 'module_manifests'`) or booted with endpoints silently missing. You now stamp the file with a format number (`SERVE_MANIFEST_FORMAT = 3`) and the building jac's version, and both readers go through one function, `read_serve_manifest()`.

prs.title: fix(config): record a ${...} form jac does not read instead of shipping it (#9184)
prs.summary: The bug: that check only sees what the config parser writes down, and the parser only understands three forms: `${VAR}`, `${VAR:-default}` and `${VAR:?message}`. The fix: the parser now matches every `${...}`.

prs.title: fix(config): stop the deploy when a shipped setting still reads ${VAR} (#8773)
prs.summary: Before this PR, a missing variable never stopped anything: the config loader caught the error and kept the literal text, so `jac scale deploy` (dry run included) shipped `${OPENAI_API_KEY}` into a Kubernetes Secret as the real API key. You made loading record every reference it could not fill in (on `JacConfig.unresolved`, with the setting's path), and you made the Kubernetes deploy refuse to…

prs.title: fix(native): include the OS reason in rmtree errors
prs.summary: Before this PR, a failed `rmtree` only said which path it could not remove, never why. The PR reads the OS error text (`errno_message()`) right after each failing system call and appends it to the error.

prs.title: fix(runtime): say why a pod does not boot from its sealed image (#9139)
prs.summary: sealed Before this PR, a pod could have a whole sealed image on disk, skip it, and compile everything from source without saying why.

prs.title: fix(scale): seal the app the deploy serves instead of the default app (#9136)
prs.summary: In a workspace (a project with several apps), the deploy always sealed the `default-app`, not the app you were deploying. You pass the name of the app the deploy serves (the fleet's `root_app`) into both sealing steps: the bake (`app=`) and the seal (`--app=`).

prs.title: fix(scale): fail the deploy when the shipped jac.toml reads env the pods will not have
prs.summary: their own The bug: a variable exported only on the deploy host made the deploy look clean, but the pod could not resolve it at boot.

prs.title: fix(dist): stop a stale runtime that will not delete from killing jac (#9053)
prs.summary: The bug: if any file inside a stale folder refused to delete, `jac` died with an uncaught error before running the user's command. The fix: `gc_stale` now wraps each stale-folder removal in `try`/`except` and prints a warning instead of crashing, and native `rmtree` now checks `unlink`, so the error names the stuck file and adds the OS reason.

prs.title: fix(config): report unresolved env vars in the command that uses them (#8773)
prs.summary: interpolation Before this PR, the code that walks the config caught that error and kept the raw text, so an unset variable became a literal value.

prs.title: fix(scale): destroy reclaims the namespace it created, and spares the one it adopted
prs.summary: Before this PR, `destroy` deleted only objects matching `managed=jac-scale,jac-scale.role in (microservice,gateway)`. You made namespace ownership something destroy can check.

prs.title: fix(scale): sanitize the configured Prometheus namespace, not just the Kubernetes fallback (#8688)
prs.summary: namespace The bug: the sanitizer only ran on the Kubernetes fallback path.

prs.title: fix(scale): the gateway streams an upload through instead of buffering it whole
prs.summary: The bug: the serving core read the whole request body into memory before routing, and the outbound client then made a second copy while sending it, so every in-flight upload cost the gateway about twice its size in RAM. The fix: the body now reaches the app as an async chunk stream, and the gateway's `forward_to` passes that stream straight to the upstream connection.

prs.title: test(scale): lock the monitoring namespace fallback so the dropped declaration cannot return (#8057)
prs.summary: The bug: `sanitize_prometheus_namespace` had an `impl` body but no `def` declaration, so the compiler dropped it. What is left here adds no product code: two regression tests in `test_config_loader.jac` that fail if the declaration disappears again, and a release note.

prs.title: fix(runtime): pool and reuse HTTP client connections (#7907)
prs.summary: Before this PR, every `arequest` call opened a brand-new TCP connection, sent `Connection: close`, and on HTTPS built a fresh TLS context (which reloads the system CA bundle). You added a per-event-loop connection pool to `arequest`.

prs.title: fix(scale): admit a single half-open probe through the circuit breaker (#7909 - Bug 2)
prs.summary: circuit breaker one

prs.title: fix(scale): record a circuit breaker failure per RPC round trip (#7909 - Bug 1)
prs.summary: circuit breaker The bug: the breaker recorded one failure only after a whole 3-attempt retry loop had failed, so it needed about 15 failed round trips (each up to a 10s timeout) to open, not 5.

prs.title: fix(scale): count every failed RPC attempt and admit one circuit breaker probe
prs.summary: circuit breaker The breaker was much weaker than its constants suggest.

prs.title: fix(scale): gate fleet readiness on the applied revision, add an opt-in full-rollout wait (#7768)
prs.summary: On a re-deploy, the old gate (`d.status.ready_replicas >= 1`) was satisfied by the previous revision's pods, so the command reported "Fleet ready" on the first poll, before the new code had a single pod running. You moved readiness into a new `rollout.jac` that only counts replicas provably from the new ReplicaSet (`available - (total - updated) >= 1`) and only after `observedGeneration` has…

prs.title: fix(runtime): keep a trailing filter separate from the hop's type filter
prs.summary: topology index The spelling `[root-->[?:A]][?val == 2]` returned every node connected to root, including unrelated `B` nodes.

prs.title: fix(scale): stop rollback from deleting a shared node on write conflict (#7605)
prs.summary: On `main`, that cleanup deleted every changed persistent node from the database, including shared nodes that already existed before the request started. Your fix makes rollback delete a node from the database only when the failed attempt created it (`anchor.hash == 0`).

prs.title: fix(scale): stop Redis eviction from dropping live event streams (#7615)
prs.summary: anchor cache event bus

prs.title: fix(runtime): restore Serializer warning occurrence counts on a threshold ladder (#7602)
prs.summary: once per process That fix removed a signal: a problem that happened once and a problem that happened a million times both produced exactly one log line.

prs.title: fix(runtime): dedup remaining per-anchor Serializer log paths (#7602)
prs.summary: Several log lines on this per-anchor read path fire every single time, so 200 reads of the same anchor give 200 identical lines, and production services saw about 23,000 lines in 5 minutes that carried only 7 lines of real information. Your PR wraps each of the eight remaining per-anchor log calls in the existing `Serializer._should_warn_once(scope, key)` gate.

prs.title: fix(scale): converge concurrent find-or-create on system_root (#7605)
prs.summary: Before this PR, every in-flight request in a process shared the very same `system_root` object (cached live in `_process_cache`). You give each request its own deep copy of the super root.

prs.title: fix(runtime): dedup Serializer unregistered-class warnings to one per class per process (#7602)
prs.summary: Before this PR, that warning was logged on every anchor read, with no dedup, so one small fixed set of problems produced an unbounded flood of identical log lines. You added one helper, `Serializer._should_warn_once(scope, key)`, backed by a process-wide set.

prs.title: fix(scale): deterministic guest root id via UUIDv5 to eliminate dangling-pointer repair (#6698)
prs.summary: Before this PR, that `root_id` was a random UUID created once, so nothing could recompute it. You replaced the random id with a computed one: `uuid5(uuid5(NAMESPACE, project_name), "__guest__")`.

prs.title: fix(scale): RedisEventStream self-heals after a stream key is evicted (#7487)
prs.summary: consumer group When Redis evicted a stream key (for example under `allkeys-lru` memory pressure), the group was destroyed along with it, but the cache still said "exists".

prs.title: feat(scale): align JWT session tokens with OIDC/RFC 7519 claims (#6068)
prs.summary: Before this PR, jac-scale session tokens put the user's UUID only in a custom `user_id` claim and had no `sub`, so standard tools (API gateways, mobile auth SDKs, OIDC relying parties) could not find the user's identity. You now emit `sub` (same value as `user_id`) and `preferred_username` in every new session token.

prs.title: fix(scale): sort MongoDB slice pushdown by _id for stable pagination (#6747)
prs.summary: The bug: `execute_plan` called `.skip()`/`.limit()` with no `.sort()` first, so MongoDB returned pages from its "natural order", which is not stable. The fix: every `execute_plan` query now runs `.sort('_id', 1)` before skip/limit.

prs.title: fix(scale): invalidate topology-index roots cross-pod on edge-list-delta (#7334)
prs.summary: root topology index

prs.title: test(scale): fix and unquarantine edge-ref slice push-down test (#6865)
prs.summary: You found it was neither: the test never reached that assertion, because the system root was never saved to MongoDB. You fixed the test harness only: the root is now registered with the tiered memory (`mem.put(ctx.system_root)`), so it is saved and reloads.

prs.title: fix(scale): eliminate redundant per-request commits in server walker path (#6699)
prs.summary: Each request ran that full O(N) scan up to three times: once when the walker finished, once while building the response, and once at context teardown. You made `commit()` the owner of the flag.

prs.title: perf(scale): reuse one MongoDB container across webhook tests (#6956)
prs.summary: Before this PR, each of the 10 "with mongo" tests started its own `mongo:latest` container, ran one check, and stopped it. You replaced the per-test container with one shared container per process.

prs.title: perf(scale): make bcrypt work factor configurable (#6956)
prs.summary: The in-process test suite boots a fresh server for every test, so every test paid about 1.5 s of bcrypt hashing for two throwaway credentials. You added a `password_hash_rounds` auth setting (default 12) and a `JAC_SCALE_BCRYPT_ROUNDS` environment variable that overrides it.

prs.title: fix(scale): bound L2 Redis memory on every deployment (#6864)
prs.summary: Only the Redis that Jac-Scale provisions itself in Kubernetes got a `maxmemory` limit and an eviction policy. Your fix makes the cache bound its own memory.

prs.title: test(jac-scale): invert obsolete redis batch test into an MGET efficiency guard (#6863)
prs.summary: The bug was in a test, not in production code: `test_redis_batch_overhead` asserted that the Redis command count grows by at least N, so it only passed while the slow per-node `GET` behaviour existed. You replaced it with a guard that asserts the opposite: reading 5 nodes and reading 25 nodes must cost about the same number of Redis read commands, and `MGET` must actually be used.

prs.title: test(jac-scale): restore connection-overhead test as efficiency guards (#6862)
prs.summary: The test still asserted that the old bugs were present, for example "expected >= 8 new connections", so it failed once CI started auto-discovering tests (#6850) and was moved to `tests/quarantine/`. You rewrote the test so it guards the correct behaviour.

prs.title: feat(jaclang): native ptr[T] typed pointers with subscript read/write (closes #6707, #6708)
prs.summary: Before this PR, `p[i]` on a pointer did not compile in either direction. `p[i]` reads become "compute address, then load".

prs.title: feat(persistence): enforce declared archetype uniqueness to stop concurrent duplicate nodes (#6266)
prs.summary: When two requests run this check-then-create on the same root at the same time, both see "missing," both create the node, and MongoDB stores two copies. You added a way to declare that an archetype is unique, `register_unique_index(UserProfile, scope="root")`.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): ignore undeclared query params on restspec endpoints (closes #4661)
prs.summary: The bug: the route builder forwarded every query parameter in the URL, including ones the endpoint never declared, so any extra parameter crashed walker and function endpoints with a 500. The fix: you added a per-endpoint flag, `forward_undeclared_query_params`, to `JEndPoint`.

prs.title: feat(persistence): eager schema migration + automatic `__jac_schema__` hook retirement
prs.summary: The gap was that these rules could never be removed. Your PR adds a three-step lifecycle to finish a migration and delete the rule.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): make node+edge create crash-atomic in Mongo sync (#6488)
prs.summary: Before this PR, `sync()` wrote objects in the order they were registered in memory. You changed `sync()` to sort pending writes into four buckets and flush them in dependency order: node documents, then edge documents, then edge-list updates on existing nodes, then plain field updates.

prs.title: feat(jac-scale): cross-pod L1 cache invalidation via Redis pub/sub (closes #6313)
prs.summary: When pod A commits a change to node X, nothing told the other live L1s, on pod A or on other pods, that their copy of X was now old. After this PR, every write publishes the anchor id on a Redis pub/sub channel (`jac:anchor:invalidate`).

prs.title: fix(jac-desktop): run desktop dev-mode tests in CI via WebKit + Xvfb, with has_display fallback (#6364)
prs.summary: Vite dev server PyTauri desktop window

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): invalidate L2 Redis cache after edge-delta atomic write (#6295)
prs.summary: The bug: after the MongoDB merge, `ScaleTieredMemory.commit()` wrote the node's old, un-merged in-memory copy into Redis, so Redis could say a node had no edges while MongoDB had the edge. The fix: `_put_node_atomic` now writes and reads back the merged edge list in one MongoDB call, repairs the in-memory anchor, and deletes the Redis entry.

prs.title: fix(testing): scope JacAPIServer config to base_path; eliminate set_config() global mutation in SPA tests
prs.summary: The SPA tests in `test_serve_client.jac` changed that shared config with `set_config(... Your fix gives each `JacAPIServer` its own config, read once at startup from its own `base_path` (plus the profile / `jac.local.toml` overlay).

prs.title: fix(mongo-backend): persist empty-dict archetype fields via $literal wrap (#6167)
prs.summary: aggregation-pipeline `$set` On MongoDB older than 6.1.0, which includes the `mongo:6.0` image jac-scale deploys, an archetype field that serialized to an empty dict (`has settings: dict = {};`, or a field cleared back to `{}`) made MongoDB reject the whole update with error 40180.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): invalidate Redis L2 cache on cascade quarantine (#6184)
prs.summary: The bug: all of that cleanup happened only in MongoDB. The fix: `MongoBackend` now holds a reference to the Redis backend (`_l2_ref`), and `_mongo_quarantine` deletes the matching Redis key after each of its three Mongo writes.

prs.title: # fix(serializer): recover non-Optional fields stored as None instead of quarantining (#6181)
prs.summary: Before this PR, if a stored field was `None` but its declared type did not allow `None` (for example `has _conv: list[dict] = []` stored as `"_conv": null`), the serializer raised a `TypeError`. 1,773 connected documents

prs.title: refactor(jac-scale): share single MongoDB container across all tests in `test_mongo_layer123.jac` (#6168)
prs.summary: testcontainers Before this PR, every one of the 13 tests started and stopped its own Docker container.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): strip empty dicts in `_put_node_atomic` to avoid MongoDB error 40180
prs.summary: MongoDB rejects that update form whenever the payload contains an empty object `{}`. You added a recursive helper, `_strip_empty_dicts`, and applied it to the non-archetype, non-edge fields (`non_arch_top`) before they go into the pipeline `$set`.

prs.title: fix(persistence): `recover_all` processes edges before nodes; silent re-link no-op on missing endpoint
prs.summary: quarantine Bug 1: `recover_all` processed quarantined records in whatever order the database returned them.

prs.title: fix(persistence): `_put_node_atomic` clobbers scalars via shallow `$mergeObjects`
prs.summary: `_put_node_atomic` wrote the walker's whole copy of the node's fields (`data.archetype`) back to Mongo, so a pod with a stale cached copy reverted fields that another pod had just written. You fixed both: `_put_node_atomic` now writes only the changed ("dirty") archetype fields as separate `data.archetype.<field>` keys, and `sync()` only sends a node there when edges were actually added or…

prs.title: fix(byllm): add httpx to jac.toml dependencies
prs.summary: PR #5944 added `httpx>=0.27.0` to `pyproject.toml` but not to `jac.toml`, so the CI dependency-alignment check failed with `[dependencies]: only in pyproject.toml -> ['httpx>=0.27.0']`. You added one line, `httpx = ">=0.27.0"`, to the `[dependencies]` section of `jac-byllm/jac.toml`, so both files list the same packages again.

prs.title: fix(persistence): cascade-quarantine edges when their node is quarantined
prs.summary: Before this PR, quarantine moved only the node. You made quarantining a node cascade: every edge whose `source` or `target` is that node is also quarantined, and its ID is removed from every live node's `data.edges`.

prs.title: perf(auth): Two-layer JWT cache + credential-epoch token revocation
prs.summary: Before this PR, a token stayed valid until its `exp` time (default 7 days), whatever happened to the account. You rewrote `validate_jwt_token` into three layers.

prs.title: fix(byllm): replace sync LLM clients with async equivalents to unblock event loop
prs.summary: synchronous The bug: `Model.model_call_no_stream`, `model_call_with_stream` and `model_call_http` used blocking clients, so a `by llm()` call made on jac-scale's single uvicorn event loop froze that loop for the whole LLM round-trip, typically 0.5–30 s.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): forward anchor arg from acommit() to commit()
prs.summary: Before this PR, `acommit()` accepted an `anchor` argument but never passed it on: it called `asyncio.to_thread(self.commit)`, so `commit()` always got `None`. You now forward the argument (`asyncio.to_thread(self.commit, anchor)`), and the `_committed` short-circuit and flag apply only when `anchor is None`, meaning a full commit.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): eliminate redundant `MongoBackend.sync()` pass per request
prs.summary: Every HTTP request committed twice, and the second commit ran synchronously on the uvicorn event loop. You added a `_committed` flag to `ScaleTieredMemory`.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): cache system root at process level to eliminate per-request MongoDB lookup
prs.summary: system root Because the in-memory cache (L1) starts empty on every request, that lookup always fell through to Redis and then MongoDB.

prs.title: fix(docs): add redirect for `internals/contrib` → `community/contributing`
prs.summary: MkDocs No page or redirect existed for that path, so anyone who clicked "contribute" from the README got a 404.

prs.title: fix(runtimelib): prevent silent topology index drops in deferred sync
prs.summary: topology index hash

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): silently drop unknown query parameters instead of crashing
prs.summary: Before this PR, any query parameter the function or walker did not declare was still passed in, so Python raised `TypeError` and the endpoint returned HTTP 500. You fixed it by reading each walker's or function's signature once, when the endpoint is registered, and then dropping every incoming key that is not in that signature before the walker or function runs.

prs.title: fix(jac-client): correct assert string and docstring placement in `test_desktop_build.jac`
prs.summary: The file never compiled, so none of its five tests ever ran. You moved each docstring to just before its `test` keyword, and changed the assert to look for `"client_only mode requires"`.

prs.title: fix(jac-client): add client_only to DesktopConfig default config
prs.summary: The bug: #5494 never added the `client_only` key to the dictionary that `get_default_config()` returns, so the existing test `test_client_only_config_is_supported` failed whenever it actually ran. The fix: you added one line, `'client_only': False`, to the dict in `get_default_config()`.

prs.title: chore: extend jac-check format enforcement to test files
prs.summary: Before this PR, the `find` command that feeds files to the formatter skipped every path containing `/tests/`, so no test file in the repo was ever format-checked. The test logic itself is unchanged in every hunk shown in the diff.

prs.title: fix(jac-scale): `pub` endpoints no longer return 401 on invalid/expired bearer tokens
prs.summary: middleware The middleware rejected every request whose bearer token failed validation with HTTP 401, before the request reached the endpoint.

prs.title: Implement Field Hash Snapshotting and Dirty Field Detection
prs.summary: Before this PR, `sync()` compared the whole in-memory object with the database copy. You changed `sync()` so it writes back only the fields this walker actually changed.

prs.title: perf(jac-scale): share testcontainers across `test_memory_hierarchy` tests to cut suite runtime
prs.summary: testcontainers Every test started its own fresh MongoDB container, and often a Redis container too, then stopped them in `finally` with an extra `time.sleep(0.5)` and `gc.collect()`.

prs.title: feat(jac-scale): partial anchor updates — skip full $set when only archetype fields changed
prs.summary: anchor archetype

prs.title: Partial Updates Implementation
prs.summary: Before this PR, a nested archetype was copied inline into its parent's blob. You added a new serializer flag, `storage_mode=True`.

prs.title: feat(jac-scale): Support custom `obj` types as walker & `@restspec` function body parameters
prs.summary: Before this PR, any field typed as a user-defined Jac `obj` collapsed to a plain `str` in the body model. You now carry the real Python type object (`type_obj`) through the parameter pipeline, build a nested Pydantic model for each Jac archetype on demand, and rebuild real archetype instances from the validated JSON before calling the handler.

prs.title: fix: resolve JWT auth timing window by moving validation into dedicated middleware
prs.summary: Per the PR description, the context started out as `system_root` (the shared root every user can reach) and only switched to the real user later, inside the endpoint, so any code that ran in between ran as the system root. You added `jwt_validation_middleware`, which runs before `request_context_middleware`.

prs.title: feat(serializer): add `ref_mode` for shared and circular object graphs
prs.summary: If an object points back to itself through other objects (for example `alice.friend = bob; bob.friend = alice`), the walk never ends and serialization recurses forever. You added an opt-in `ref_mode=True` flag.

prs.title: Custom Object Support
prs.summary: Before this PR, any type name that was not a built-in primitive silently became `str`, so a walker with `has user: User;` exposed `user` as a plain string and could not accept a JSON object. You made `_get_python_type` look up the Jac class by name, build a matching Pydantic model from its `init` signature (nested models included), and convert the validated model back into a real Jac object…

prs.title: fix: prevent unnecessary DB writes on read-only operations (Redis L2 cache path)
prs.summary: anchor The flag was wrong in both directions.

prs.title: Fix: Prevent unnecessary saves in ScaleTieredMemory
prs.summary: Before this PR, `commit()` wrote every persistent, writable anchor in L1 to L3 and L2 on every request, even when the walker changed nothing. You added an `is_updated` "dirty" flag to `Anchor`, set it automatically whenever a public archetype field is assigned (or an edge is added or removed), and changed `commit()` so that only anchors with `is_updated = True` are written to MongoDB and Redis.

prs.title: fix: correct ExecutionContext field types to non-optional
prs.summary: They were declared as `NodeAnchor | None` ("an anchor or nothing"), but `postinit` always fills them with a real anchor. The final PR removes `| None` from the three field annotations in `jac/jaclang/runtimelib/context.jac`, so code that reads them no longer needs null guards.

prs.title: Fix: Walker Route OpenAPI Parameter Naming Inconsistency
prs.summary: The route's path variable and its declared parameter had different names: the parameter was declared as `node`, but the path and the handler used `nd`. You renamed the declared parameter from `node` to `nd` in all three places that create it: static walker endpoints, and the dynamic POST and GET walker endpoints.

prs.title: Fix: Include `redis.conf.template` in package distribution

You added one glob pattern, `"providers/
